reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or exact location for individual Azure data center campuses, including this facility in Medina County. The San Antonio region hosts multiple Microsoft data centers spanning Bexar and Medina counties, with expansion ongoing amid state-level debate over data center growth in Texas. Without disclosed specifications, this campus cannot be evaluated against the published benchmarks used to assess other facilities.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 18 operators have published power capacity figures totaling 468 megawatts. This campus would rank 19th by published capacity if its specifications were disclosed, meaning it falls below the threshold of operators who provide this data. The absence of a published figure does not indicate the facility's size or readiness.

For readers assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the lack of disclosure means it cannot be weighed against known constraints. Microsoft's policy of publishing only worldwide aggregate statistics creates a systematic gap in visibility into individual campus capacity. The facility exists and is part of Microsoft's expanding Azure infrastructure in Texas, but its contribution to regional and national AI compute supply remains opaque.
